changes.summary: Schefter's trade speculation no longer calls two teams division rivals unless they actually share a division.
AFL Rosters on a phone: position headers span the full card again, and the sort chips scroll inside it and read like TheLeague's ("Pts ↓").
Quieter GroupMe: the Pecking Order and Gauntlet posts are now one line and a link, and trade rumors stay in the news feed and opt-in push alerts.
Franchise pages now follow each team through MFL renumbering: the SeaBirds keep their 2023–24 seasons, and no team shows another team’s old seasons.
Homepage My Team card shows this week in season: whether your lineup is set (and who's on bye or out), your record, next opponent, and one-tap Set Lineup, Free Agents, Trade Builder and Roster.
Homepage My Team card shows this week in season: whether your lineup is set (and who's on bye or out), your record, next opponent, and one-tap Set Lineup, Free Agents, Trade Builder and Roster.
The menu now opens with the pages you use most — Roster, Set Lineup, Live Scoring, Free Agents, Standings, Trade Builder and Tip Schefter — pinned at the top all year.
The pages you use most now end with a card of related pages — Sunday Ticket on Live Scoring, Schedule and Playoffs on Standings, Ask Roger on Rules, and more.
The homepage now spotlights the season's top scorer, with a one-tap link to Top Players.
Player sheet on Rosters: Trade block moved into the ⋮ menu with a label, the trade icon and a ✓ when he's on the block — the old unlabelled circle looked like it did nothing.
Player sheet on Rosters: This Week's Projected shows the projection alone again, instead of every stat run together.
Player sheet on Rosters: Recent weeks leaves out a week with no score instead of printing "W2 -".
Search: results now rank by what owners actually open, so Tip Schefter and Set Lineup come up before rarely used pages.
Owner Activity: moved pages like Draft Room are no longer listed as never opened, and articles and franchise pages show their names.
Roster and transaction moves made on MFL's own site now show up here within a minute, down from two.
A new front-page homepage with your weekly rivalry pinned to the headlines, plus a slimmer header that carries this week's scores across the top of every page.
changes.headline: Archie's gets a front page
changes.lede: The homepage now reads like a sports front page: the week's lead story, your rivalry with this week's opponents, the latest moves and the race at the top of the standings.
changes.imageAlt: Archie's new homepage with the score strip, your team band, the Gauntlet lead story and top headlines

changes.summary: Standings got a new look: division leaders up top, a playoff picture of who is in and who is chasing, and all-play with a luck column.
Standings now match the front page: team-colour division leaders, a MAD POWER 99 playoff picture and an all-play luck column.
Free Agents now opens on the best available player at each position, with the most added and most dropped players this week beside the list.
A new, lighter icon style across the site, with clearer menu icons for Roster, Live Scoring, the draft pages and more — and Tip Schefter now wears Schefter himself.
A new, lighter icon style across the site, with clearer icons in the menu for Roster, Live Scoring, the draft pages, Throwback Week and more.
The Rosters icon now wears number 16, one for each of the AFL's roster spots.
The Live Scoring icon now reads 0-3, for the league founded in '03.
The Live Scoring icon now reads 0-7.
The home page headline now reads "Nine divisions. One champ." instead of stopping at "One."
The home page headline now reads "Two conferences. One champ." instead of stopping at "One."
Schefter can no longer use another league's name in AFL news, chat posts or notifications; the Week 5 Gauntlet headline now says the AFL.
Rosters on a phone now show player cards instead of a sideways-scrolling table, the same as the AFL.
Transactions is now Schefter's wire: every move gets his write-up, with the official record under See details, and past seasons tucked in a menu.
changes.headline: Schefter now reports every move
changes.lede: The Transactions page leads with Claude Schefter's take on each pickup, cut and trade this season. Tap See details for MFL's official record.
changes.imageAlt: The Transactions page showing Schefter's write-ups of the day's pickups, one opened to show the official record
